text.en: The Kallanai dam built by Karikala Chola in the 2nd century still waters the Kaveri delta. Our ancestors knew how to manage water and energy.

Non-conventional energy sources are renewable and clean: solar, biogas, wind, water, tidal, biomass and geothermal.
Solar cells (silicon photovoltaic devices) convert sunlight directly to electricity; many cells form a solar panel; solar cookers and heaters use sunlight directly.
Biogas (about 75 percent methane) is produced from cow dung and wastes in the absence of oxygen; it burns smokelessly and leaves rich manure.
Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of wind into electricity and pumping; it is free and pollution free.
Hydropower uses falling water, while tidal energy uses the rise and fall of ocean tides to turn turbines.
Shale gas is extracted by hydraulic fracturing, which can contaminate groundwater and uses a lot of water.
Rainwater harvesting stores rain to recharge groundwater, using roof tops, recharge pits, eris and ooranis.
Eris are interconnected tanks in Tamil Nadu; ooranis are small ponds; the Grand Anicut (Kallanai) was built by Karikala Chola in the 2nd century CE.
Save electricity with CFL and LED bulbs, switching off unused appliances and using solar water heaters.

problem.en: List the advantages and one limitation of solar energy.

text.en: It is abundant, free, renewable and pollution free.
It is used for electricity or heating.
The limitation is that solar panels are expensive to make and work only in sunlight.

prompt.en: How does rooftop rainwater harvesting raise groundwater?

requiredIdeas.en: Roof rain is piped to a filter
Water percolates to the water table

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking it only stores water in tanks
